## Finding F002-i2 #1 (high, correctness) — addressed

The auditor showed disclaimer attribution allowed false negatives in two shapes. I replaced the flat "nearest non-neutral neighbour on either side" model in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/doc_drift.py` with deterministic per-mention attribution over **typed separators**:

- **Parentheses are now strong segment boundaries** (`_SEPARATOR_RE`), so `Gemini is a shipped executor (Grok is operator-only).` splits into a claim segment and a disclaimer segment instead of one mixed segment that `_segment_class`'s disclaimer-wins rule laundered. Gemini now sits in the claim segment and flags.
- **Separators carry strength** (`_split_unit`): coordinating conjunctions (`and/or/nor`) are weak; sentence ends, commas, dashes, parens, and contrast conjunctions are strong; adjacent runs like `, and` merge with strong winning. A neutral mention first binds to its own clause across weak links (`_weakly_reached`): a weakly-reached claim is drift, a weakly-reached disclaimer is honest — this is what keeps the corrected README's `Gemini and Grok are operator-only runtimes` passing even though the `and`-split isolates "Gemini".
- **Strong-boundary fallback requires an un-owned disclaimer** (`_owned_by_other`): a mention may only be excu
